answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut is aggressive, but memory_c4 demonstrated that renegotiation against market benchmarks recovered real margin at renewal without service erosion. With 14 days to renewal and 94% line utilization leaving no buffer for supply disruption, switching vendors or deferring creates unacceptable delivery risk. memory_c1 and memory_c6 show the incumbent has delivered stable integration and unlocked volume pricing on multi-year terms. Verifying memory_c4's renegotiation outcome will confirm whether aggressive benchmarking can close the 18% gap or identify the realistic negotiation ceiling. If the incumbent cannot meet 18%, we retain the option to escalate to a second source or vendor switch in the next cycle with full visibility. Renewal buys time without locking in cost structure—memory_c5 precedent shows month-to-month extensions are viable if needed. This approach preserves supply continuity under extreme utilization pressure while testing the cost target against proven negotiation leverage.
